newsitem.title: GERMANY: ATHLETICS-IAAF TO PROBE FIGHT OVER DOPING TESTS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-IAAF TO PROBE FIGHT OVER DOPING TESTS.

text.p: International athletics officials have launched an investigation into a fight which broke out when a drug tester tried to take urine samples from Greek athletes in Germany last week.

The International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) said on Tuesday it was studying a report from one of its drug testers who alleges he was pushed about by an angry Greek coach when he was trying to carry out random training tests in Dortmund.

The doping official was unable to take any urine samples for analysis and the Greek athletes could face a four-year ban if they are found guilty of having refused to provide them, the equivalent of testing positive for banned substances under IAAF rules.
But there is confusion about whether the tester involved identified both himself and the athletes properly.
"We have been surprised by this incident. It is not every day that it ends up in a sort of fight," IAAF general secretary Istvan Gyulai said from the governing body's headquarters in Monaco.
"We have a written report from the sample officer and we have talked to the Greeks but we are still waiting for their report."
Under IAAF rules a drug tester must identify himself to athletes with written ID before he attempts to carry out any tests.
In this case it appears that tester Klaus Wengoborski told the Greek coach that he was from doping control but claims he did not have time to show his identification before a scuffle broke out.
He was unable to get any tests from the athletes before they left the arena.

"I believe there has been a fatal misunderstanding," Gyulai said. "The sample officer did not produce an ID card...The official said he was from doping control. The Greek coach says he did not know who was."

The case could turn out to be a huge embarrassment to Greece, who are due to host the world outdoor championships in Athens in August. It is also likely to end up in a long-running battle over rules and technicalities.
Athletics sources said it was unclear if the doping officer was able to identify all the Greek athletes he was due to test.
Technically they may not be able to be accused of dodging tests if they were not approached individually and could not be clearly identified by the tester.
